name: Sociological Perspectives on Organisations
description: This course trains students to understand the social dynamics of different types of organisations, with a focus on practices of work and the making of workplaces. While familiarising students with the theoretical approaches and concepts necessary to understand the individual’s relationship to the organisation, it will enable students to think critically about questions of identity, agency, power and control in organisational spaces. We discuss the interface of culture, ways of thinking, feeling, acting and being in different organisations. This enables a shift from the managerial perspectives and psycho-social views of organisations, and draws out the complex negotiations and tensions endemic to organisational life. The course also draws on literature on different types of organisations such as corporations, hospitals, and prisons to elaborate the unique cultural configurations in these spaces and contexts.
